title: SOUTHCOM: tic tac detected by space asset near a naval vessel

tellings.quote: Southcom southern command tic tac detected by space asset in proximity of vessel.

plain: A Tic Tac, a white oval object shaped like the mint, was picked up by a sensor in space as it passed close to a ship at sea, in the area covered by the US military's Southern Command. Jesse Michels reads out this case heading on the show with Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, and it comes from the Immaculate Constellation report, an unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Representative Nancy Mace entered into the record of a House Oversight hearing on 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon. The report calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Brown later said he wrote it, and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report describes imagery of "a Tic-Tac UAP" (UAP is the official term for unexplained objects) "transiting through an area of the Atlantic Ocean", says "No observed reaction is seen to come from the vessel", and reads the ship's nearness as a sign of "foreknowledge of the UAP event by intelligence". If so, someone would have known in advance where the object would be, but that is the report's own inference, and the imagery is described, not shown.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report's case "SOUTHCOM Tic-Tac Detected by Space Asset in Proximity of Vessel" describes "OPIR imagery and MASINT of a Tic-Tac UAP transiting through an area of the Atlantic Ocean" and says "No observed reaction is seen to come from the vessel", reading the vessel's nearness as a sign of "foreknowledge of the UAP event by intelligence". Jesse Michels reads out the heading; that the vessel knew in advance is the report's own inference, and the imagery is described, not shown.
